summary: During its active phase the port is an essentially exact reproduction (event rate, instant-attack/2.6 s decay envelope, spatial independence, 4-slot picker wiring, hue mapping, rig scaling all match to seed noise), but it fails to reproduce two authentic reference behaviours: the original's deterministic 32.80 s total freeze that recurs every 114.65 s at 20 fps (27.3% of runtime, now known to be genuine PB add-wrap behaviour), and two of the four untouched default hues (tertiary 28.7 deg vs 21.5 deg, quaternary 50.3 deg vs 39.5 deg).
observations: Same visual idea on both sides (60 px strip, default rig): independent per-pixel twinkles with an instant attack (peak is always the event's first frame) and a smooth decay, no lateral motion — waterfalls are strictly vertical bars on both sides. Palette is red/orange/amber with meanB exactly 0 and mean saturation 1.000 on both; peak channel values top out at 253 (orig) / 249 (port).

THE ORIGINAL'S FREEZE IS DETERMINISTIC, LARGE, AND THE PORT NEVER REPRODUCES IT. At 20 fps over 1200 s (24000 frames, rj-long20-1200) the orig is byte-identical frame-to-frame for exactly 32.80 s starting at t = 81.80, 196.45, 311.10, 425.75, 540.40, 655.00, 769.65, 884.30, 998.95 and 1113.60 s — ten stalls, period 114.65 s (one 114.60 s gap), 6560/24000 frames = 27.3% of the run completely static. The port had ZERO zero-motion runs of even 0.3 s in the same 24000 frames. Confirmed visually: rj-regime-frozen (--skip 85 --seconds 20 --fps 20) gives the orig 400/400 zero-motion frames with meanBrightness min == max == 14 and a perfectly static striped waterfall, while the port animates normally through the identical window.

The freeze cadence is frame-rate dependent but its DURATION is a fixed 32.80 s of simulated time at every rate. Measured onsets/periods on the orig: 5 fps — onset 38.40 s, period 71.3 s (stalls at 38.40/109.80/181.00/252.40); 10 fps — onset 46.70 s, period 79.6 s (46.70/126.30/205.80/285.40); 20 fps — onset 81.80 s, period 114.65 s. In every case period minus 32.80 s equals the onset, i.e. the pattern runs for <onset> seconds, holds absolutely still for 32.80 s, and repeats. AT 40 fps THE ORIGINAL DOES NOT FREEZE AT ALL within 500 s (rj-fps40-500, 20000 frames, longest zero-motion run 0.55 s) — so the freeze regime is present at 5/10/20 fps and absent at 40 fps. The port never freezes at 5, 10, 20 or 40 fps.

The freeze is not seed-, rig-size- or dial-dependent on the original: onset is exactly t = 81.80 s with duration 32.80 s at seed 1, seed 7 and seed 1234; at 12 px, 60 px and 300 px; and with all four hsvPickers explicitly dialed to 0/120/240/300 deg (rj-dialed-4hue). The port stalls in none of those configurations.

OUTSIDE the freeze the two sides are statistically indistinguishable. Over the 1200 s / 20 fps run, restricting the orig to its 17440 non-frozen frames: orig meanR 42.30, meanG 8.61, meanB 0.00, meanBrightness 16.97, motionLit 1.48 vs port (all 24000 frames) meanR 42.17, meanG 10.63, meanB 0.00, meanBrightness 17.60, motionLit 1.55. The only residual colour gap is the +23% green from the wrong default hues (next observation); red and blue match.

DEFAULT HUES DIVERGE IN SLOTS 3 AND 4. Untouched 60 s / 20 fps dump (rj-dump-default, 60 sampled frames, bright pixels max-channel >= 150): orig hue clusters at 0.0, 10.6, 21.5 and 39.5 deg; port at 0.0, 10.6, 28.7 and 50.3 deg. In PB hue units (0..1) that is orig 0 / 0.030 / 0.060 / 0.110 vs port 0 / 0.030 / 0.080 / 0.140. Slots 1 and 2 agree exactly; slots 3 and 4 sit 7.2 deg and 10.8 deg too far toward yellow, which is why the port's untouched strip reads slightly more golden/amber and the original more pure red-orange.

EVENT STATISTICS MATCH. From a dense 800-consecutive-frame dump (rj-dense-4hue, 40 s at 20 fps, all four pickers dialed to 0/120/240/300 deg, onset = max-channel jump > 20 and > 60): orig 465 events = 0.194 events/px/s, median event duration 2.65 s, median peak value 140; port 483 events = 0.201 events/px/s, median duration 2.60 s, median peak 132.

DECAY ENVELOPE IS ESSENTIALLY IDENTICAL. Normalising each strong event (peak > 150) to its first frame and averaging over 200+ events per side, the envelope sampled every 0.2 s is orig 1.000 0.912 0.828 0.749 0.673 0.601 0.533 0.470 0.410 0.354 0.303 0.255 0.212 0.173 0.137 and port 1.000 0.911 0.826 0.746 0.669 0.597 0.529 0.465 0.406 0.351 0.299 0.252 0.209 0.169 0.135 — max deviation 0.004 across the whole 2.8 s decay.

COLOUR-SLOT SELECTION PROBABILITIES MATCH. Classifying all 465/483 event onsets in rj-dense-4hue by hue: orig 29.2% / 31.0% / 36.3% / 3.4% for slots 1-4, port 30.8% / 28.4% / 37.5% / 3.3%. The rare fourth slot (~3%) is reproduced correctly, and is why its probe delta is the smallest on both sides.

CONTROL SURFACE MATCHES EXACTLY: both sides expose hsvPickerPrimary/Secondary/Tertiary/Quaternary, all kind hsvPicker, labels Primary/Secondary/Tertiary/Quaternary. Probe called all four responsive on both sides (orig maxDeltaLit 16.18 / 10.66 / 11.27 / 4.11; port 15.31 / 12.77 / 16.24 / 1.17).

SLOT WIRING IS CORRECT ON EVERY DIAL. Setting exactly one picker to 0.6667 (blue) and histogramming bright-pixel hues: on the orig, Primary moves the 0 deg population, Secondary the 10.6 deg, Tertiary the 21.5 deg, Quaternary the 39.5 deg — one population to 240 deg per dial, the other three untouched. The port does the same with its own defaults (Primary 0, Secondary 10.6, Tertiary 28.7, Quaternary 50.3). No cross-wiring or slot reordering.
HUE MAPPING IS EXACT AND IDENTICAL ACROSS THE FULL RANGE: dialing hsvPickerPrimary to 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75 / 0.90 produces measured hues of exactly 90 / 180 / 270 / 324 deg on BOTH sides.

S AND V COMPONENTS OF THE PICKERS ARE IGNORED ON BOTH SIDES, identically: hsvPickerPrimary = 0.5,1,0.25 and 0.5,0.3,1 both render BYTE-IDENTICAL to 0.5,1,1 on orig and on port (4 dumped frames over a 10 s window each).

PER-PIXEL DENSITY LAW IS RIG-SIZE INDEPENDENT ON BOTH SIDES: at 12 / 60 / 300 px over 150 s at 20 fps both sides keep the same per-pixel event character; no side changes feature width or rate with strip length, and the orig's freeze fires at the same t = 81.80 s at all three sizes.

NEITHER SIDE IS FRAME-RATE COUPLED IN ITS EVENT RATE — the twinkle density and decay read the same at 5, 10, 20 and 40 fps on both sides. The only fps-sensitive behaviour found anywhere is the original's freeze machinery (present 5/10/20 fps, absent at 40 fps).

Survey note: the 60 s / 5 fps survey shows the orig dying at t ~ 38 s and staying dead for the rest of the window while the port twinkles throughout. That is the real freeze, not a low-fps survey artefact — it reproduces at 3, 5, 10 and 20 fps and was confirmed at 20 fps by direct frame dumps.

dials.name: hsvPickerPrimary
dials.origEffect: Sets the hue of colour slot 1, which is picked for ~29% of twinkle events. Hue is honoured exactly: 0.25/0.50/0.75/0.90 render as 90/180/270/324 deg. Saturation and value components are ignored (s=0.3 and v=0.25 render byte-identical to s=1,v=1). Untouched default hue 0.0 deg.
dials.portEffect: Identical in every respect: same exact hue mapping (90/180/270/324 deg), same ~31% event share, S and V likewise ignored, same untouched default hue 0.0 deg.

dials.name: hsvPickerSecondary
dials.origEffect: Hue of colour slot 2, ~31% of events. Setting it to 0.6667 moves exactly the 10.6 deg population to 240 deg and leaves 0/21.5/39.5 deg untouched. S/V ignored. Untouched default hue 10.6 deg.
dials.portEffect: Identical mapping and share (~28%); setting 0.6667 moves exactly the 10.6 deg population to 240 deg. Untouched default hue also 10.6 deg. S/V ignored.

dials.name: hsvPickerTertiary
dials.origEffect: Hue of colour slot 3, the most-picked slot at ~36% of events. Setting 0.6667 moves exactly the 21.5 deg population to 240 deg. S/V ignored. Untouched default hue 21.5 deg (PB units 0.060).
dials.portEffect: Correct slot wiring and matching share (~37.5%), and once dialed the behaviour is indistinguishable — but the UNTOUCHED DEFAULT is 28.7 deg (PB units 0.080) instead of 21.5 deg.

dials.name: hsvPickerQuaternary
dials.origEffect: Hue of the rare colour slot 4 — only ~3.4% of events, hence the smallest probe delta (maxDeltaLit 4.11). Setting 0.6667 moves exactly the 39.5 deg population to 240 deg. S/V ignored. Untouched default hue 39.5 deg (PB units 0.110).
dials.portEffect: Correct slot wiring and same rarity (~3.3% of events, probe maxDeltaLit 1.17); dialed behaviour indistinguishable — but the UNTOUCHED DEFAULT is 50.3 deg (PB units 0.140) instead of 39.5 deg.

feedback: PRIMARY GAP — reproduce the original's periodic total freeze. Oracle probing (2026-08-29) established that plain add/'+=' wraps at the 16.16 range ends on real Pixel Blaze hardware, so the original's stall is AUTHENTIC reference behaviour, not an engine bug: the port is missing it. Target behaviour at 20 fps on the default 60 px strip: animate normally for 81.80 s, then hold the last frame absolutely still (motion exactly 0, meanBrightness min == max) for exactly 32.80 s, then resume, with a 114.65 s period. The stall duration is a fixed 32.80 s of simulated time at every frame rate, and the active phase equals the onset: 38.40 s at 5 fps (period 71.3 s), 46.70 s at 10 fps (period 79.6 s), 81.80 s at 20 fps (period 114.65 s), and NO stall at all within 500 s at 40 fps. The port currently shows zero stalls of even 0.3 s over 24000 frames (1200 s at 20 fps) at seeds 1/7/1234, at 12/60/300 px, and with all pickers dialed. Almost certainly the port has replaced a wrapping accumulator with a clamping/modulo/reset one, or is stepping a per-pixel timer by an amount that never reaches the wrap point.

SECONDARY GAP — fix the two wrong default hues. The port's built-in colour set is 0 / 10.6 / 28.7 / 50.3 deg; the original's is 0 / 10.6 / 21.5 / 39.5 deg. In Pixel Blaze hue units that is port 0 / 0.030 / 0.080 / 0.140 vs original 0 / 0.030 / 0.060 / 0.110 — lower the tertiary default from ~0.08 to ~0.06 and the quaternary from ~0.14 to ~0.11. Verify with an untouched 60 s / 20 fps dump: bright pixels (max channel >= 150) should cluster at 0.0, 10.6, 21.5 and 39.5 deg, and the active-phase meanG should fall from ~10.6 to ~8.6 with meanR unchanged at ~42.2 and meanB at 0.

DO NOT TOUCH ANYTHING ELSE ABOUT THE COLOUR SYSTEM. The hue mapping is exact over the full 0..1 range (0.25/0.50/0.75/0.90 -> 90/180/270/324 deg on both sides), the S and V components of every picker are correctly ignored (byte-identical renders at s=0.3 and v=0.25), each control drives the correct slot, and the four slots are chosen with matching probabilities (orig 29.2/31.0/36.3/3.4 % vs port 30.8/28.4/37.5/3.3 % over 465/483 events).

DO NOT change the twinkle timing, density or decay. Event rate (orig 0.194 vs port 0.201 events/px/s), instant attack, median event duration (2.65 vs 2.60 s), median peak value (140 vs 132), the normalised decay envelope (identical to within 0.004 over 2.8 s), 1-px-dominant feature width, spatial independence between neighbouring pixels, and the rate's independence from strip length (checked at 12/60/300 px) all match the original to within seed noise. Any 'fix' that shifts these would be a regression.

When re-verifying, do it at 20 fps over at least 250 s (two full freeze cycles) — a 6 s baseline or a 60 s survey lands entirely inside the active phase at 20 fps and will show a perfect match while the real gap sits at t = 81.8-114.6 s. Also re-check at 40 fps, where the ORIGINAL does not freeze either: a port fix must not introduce a stall at rates where the original has none.
